title: Thou, Whose Almighty Word
description: Thou, Whose Almighty Word in Tonic Solfa to DORT, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: John Marriott wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 174, “Let There Be Light”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sixes and Fours (6.6.4.6.6.6.4) (6.6.4.6.6.6.4), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to DORT; any other Sixes and Fours (6.6.4.6.6.6.4) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Thou, whose al-might-y word Cha-os and dark-ness heard, And took their flight! Hear us, we hum-bly pray, And where the gos-pel day Sheds not its glo-rious ray, Let there be light!

lines: Thou, who didst come to bring,
Health to the sick in mind,
Through the world, far and wide,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: John Marriott died in 1825.
credits: Words by John Marriott (1780–1825), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to DORT by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
